challenges.name: revalidate-tags-quiz
challenges.title: Which cached entries does this edit make wrong?
challenges.description: Two server actions from the instructor dashboard and the tags of the catalog's cached reads: decide whether each action refreshes what the edit made wrong.

questions.explanation: True. The description is stored in exactly one cached read, getCourse, tagged course:<id>. The card reads select title, price, slug and category, so no card entry contains the old description. Expiring the list and category tags as well would rebuild the catalog and the category page with identical content: cost without benefit. The misconception is that an edit to a course must refresh every page that mentions the course; the question to ask is which cached data contains the changed field.

False. Tags are compared as whole strings: the react entry was stored with courses:category:react only, and no call expired that tag. The log confirms it: the react page was served from the cache at 10:02:19 and still lists the course, and it will keep doing so until its time-based lifetime ends. The fix is to read the course before the update and also expire courses:category:<old category>. The misconception is that tags form a hierarchy, so that a "list" tag covers the category lists whose names look related.

challenges.name: revalidation-targets
challenges.title: Revalidate exactly what an edit made wrong
challenges.description: After an instructor moved a course to another category, the old category page kept listing it; the hotfix revalidated the whole site after every save. Write revalidationTargets(catalog, event): the tags for revalidateTag and the paths for revalidatePath that one domain event makes necessary, no more and no less. Conventions: course:<id> holds every field of one course and is read by its page /course/<slug>; courses:list (the catalog /courses) and courses:category:<category> (one category page) hold the cards of published courses only, which show title, price, slug, category and the instructor's name; instructor:<id> holds the instructor's name for course pages; the category sidebar of /courses has no tag, so only the path /courses refreshes it. The catalog is the state before the event; each course has id, slug, title, description, price, category, instructorId and published. Rules. course_updated { courseId, changes } (changes may hold title, description, price, category, slug; any other key is ignored) and price_changed { courseId, price } (the same as changes { price }): a field counts as changed only when its new value differs from the catalog value; no changed field -> nothing. Otherwise course:<id>; if the course is published and a card field (title, price, slug, category) changed, also courses:list and courses:category:<current category>; if the category changed (published), also courses:category:<new category> and the path /courses; if the slug changed (published), the paths /course/<old slug> and /course/<new slug>. lesson_added { courseId, lessonId } -> course:<id>. course_published / course_unpublished { courseId }: when the course is already in that state -> nothing; otherwise course:<id>, courses:list, courses:category:<category> and the paths /course/<slug> and /courses. instructor_renamed { instructorId, name } -> instructor:<instructorId>, plus courses:list and courses:category:<c> for every category c of a published course of that instructor. An unknown courseId or event type -> nothing. Return { tags, paths }, each without duplicates and sorted with the default string sort. The runner checks every event on its own against the same catalog and prints a JSON array with one { tags, paths } per event.
hints: For each event, ask two questions: which fields really changed (compared with the catalog, not just sent by the form), and which cached reads show those fields? A tag belongs in the answer only if the answer to the second question includes it.

Look at what the old state gives you: the current category and slug come from the catalog, the new ones from the event, and an edit that moves a course between categories or URLs makes both the old and the new one wrong. Collect everything into two Sets and sort at the end, so duplicates and order take care of themselves.

A similar mapping for a different feature: lessons are cached under lesson:<id> (title, body) and module:<moduleId> (lesson titles only). Renaming a lesson changes a field the module list shows, so it gives ["lesson:5", "module:2"]; editing only the body gives ["lesson:5"]; moving lesson 5 from module 2 to module 3 gives ["lesson:5", "module:2", "module:3"]; saving the same title again gives [].
